method.interaction: CUA IAB browser; disposable audit-origin description only. Product source inspection and selected official documentation.
limits: Agent walkthrough, not a human usability study.
No analyzers installed or executed; no performance or accuracy benchmark.

Live checks focused on mixed-language builder and Windows source/binary transition; Java, dependency/container and temporal adoption were inspected in existing profiles/guides rather than re-running the newcomer walkthrough.
No external privacy behavior was network-captured; upstream statements are documentation evidence only.

scenarios.task: Python backend, TypeScript client, HTTP API
scenarios.inputs: Backend Python/source-only; client TypeScript/source-only; OpenAPI connection with test endpoint available.
scenarios.outcome: Component and connection results remained separate. Python source produced Bandit/detect-secrets/mypy/Pylint/Pyright/Ruff; client produced detect-secrets/ESLint; API produced Schemathesis, RESTler, ZAP and Burp edition candidates before cost filtering. No unsupported inference from language to API capability observed.

scenarios.inputs: Any continuing free option plus Open source.
scenarios.outcome: Burp Professional and Community were removed for the corresponding cost/license restrictions; other reviewed candidates remained. Eligibility caveat is visible. No cross-edition capability mixing observed.

scenarios.inputs: Named system Agent 7 disposable adoption audit; selected Ruff, mypy and Schemathesis for comparison; reloaded.
scenarios.outcome: System components/connections/preferences persisted; temporary comparison choices cleared as the UI explicitly promises. This is not a persistence defect.

scenarios.inputs: C++, native executable, Windows host and target, binaries only, rebuild No, instrumentation No, workload Yes.
scenarios.outcome: Dr. Memory remained a recorded match; Valgrind Memcheck/Helgrind were excluded. Binwalk/cwe-checker asked for external host verification. ASan was not offered as a ready binary-only route.

scenarios.inputs: Added source; rebuild Yes; instrumentation Yes; workload Yes.
scenarios.outcome: AddressSanitizer became a recorded match and displayed its instrumentation/rebuild condition. More source analyzers appeared. The result refresh is debounced; an immediate snapshot can precede the settled result.

scenarios.inputs: Read Java source/bytecode guide, OSV/Grype/Trivy profiles, and temporal workflow guide.
scenarios.outcome: Guidance separates artifacts and evidence scope well, but production adoption and persistent decision records remain manual.

findings.title: Add the handoff from a local check to repeatable CI result handling
findings.user_task: Adopt a shortlisted tool in a project without treating analyzer failure as a clean result.
findings.evidence: The Ruff first try and project section explain selected rules and fixes but do not explain exit states or artifact retention. The CI/CD research note deliberately provides considerations, not a tested connector. Existing workflow guides emphasize preserving failures/configuration, but there is no maintained adoption procedure showing how a concrete tool's successful run, detected findings and setup failure are handled differently in CI.

external_evidence.support: Official Ruff docs distinguish status 0, finding status 1, and abnormal/configuration failure status 2, and document flags that alter finding/fix exit behavior. This supports a concrete scoped example rather than a universal exit-code rule.
Official OSV-Scanner usage documents output-file/format controls and pre-commit integration. The exact integration contract is tool-specific.

findings.impact: Engineers must reconstruct result/error handling, retention and gating after the wiki has helped them choose tools. A green pipeline alone may conceal disabled checks or mishandled failure states.
findings.confidence: High for documented gap; impact is reviewer assessment, not an observed user failure.
findings.recommendation: Add a single adoption how-to linked from the existing research note and a representative profile. Start with the planned Python recipe: explicit tool/configuration versions, scope, retained report/log artifacts, differentiated run states and a deliberately chosen gate. Keep each tool's exact return-code and output contract linked to primary documentation. Do not turn the research note into an untested production connector.
acceptance_criteria: A reader can distinguish completed no-findings, completed findings, and execution/configuration failure for the chosen example.
The example records the analyzed revision, configuration and tool version, and preserves failure logs as well as reports.
Gate behavior and any baseline/suppression policy are stated rather than inferred from nonzero exit alone.
Keep the example illustrative until a later authorized hands-on validation records execution evidence.
Reuse the first-result fixture/run-record work; avoid a second competing recipe system.
findings.prior_audit_status: Extends the existing CI/CD research considerations and prior integration-field proposal; not a regression.
findings.compatibility: Documentation first; no saved-system or URL-format changes required.

findings.title: Make execution, network and data boundaries comparable
findings.user_task: Choose a workflow for private code or a network-restricted environment.
findings.evidence: Comparison exposes host environment, cost and licensing but no consistent workflow-specific account/network/data boundary. OSV-Scanner mentions online lookup versus prepared offline data; Semgrep Code says managed or local/CI scanning and CE is separated by license/scope, but those distinctions do not by themselves explain rule retrieval, metrics or platform submission. No incorrect upload assertion was found.

external_evidence.support: The official policy distinguishes Registry/login-dependent metrics, local-rule use, and explicitly platform-connected findings data. Therefore a local scanner label alone does not describe all network behavior.
Official usage distinguishes package extraction and vulnerability matching, and links offline mode using prepared cached data.

findings.impact: An engineer cannot consistently compare adoption fit for restricted environments from free/open-source labels or host OS. They must reconstruct the boundaries independently for each candidate.
findings.confidence: High for content inconsistency; no network traffic or privacy failure tested.
findings.recommendation: Start with reviewed per-workflow prose for Semgrep CE/Code and OSV-Scanner/Trivy/Grype: execution location, required service/account, rule/database retrieval, optional metrics/result submission, and offline preparation limitations. State unknowns. Consider comparison metadata only after these facts have been reviewed consistently; do not infer confidentiality or offline suitability from licensing.
acceptance_criteria: Separate where analysis runs from what network access or platform submission a chosen workflow uses.
Separate required operations from optional metrics, reports and remote integrations.
Link dated official evidence and retain edition/mode qualifications.
Explain offline preparation and freshness limits without claiming an untested air-gapped configuration works.
No privacy certification, blanket no-upload claim, or unsupported binary filter is introduced.
dependencies: Workflow-level evidence review before adding structured filters
findings.prior_audit_status: Extends prior platform/interface/integration proposal with a concrete adoption decision.
findings.compatibility: Documentation-first; any later fields should be optional and must not reinterpret existing v1 saved descriptions.

findings.title: Give external compatibility questions a different next action from missing fields
findings.user_task: Resolve a candidate's compatibility caveat when the actual host OS is already supplied.
reproduce: Create a C++ component with Binaries only, Native executable, Windows host/target, no rebuild/instrumentation, and a runnable workload.
Read Binwalk or cwe-checker candidate's Verify analysis host OS message.
Observe the Answer for component control even though the Windows selection is already present; source routes that action to the same selector.
findings.evidence: Live UI asks 'Verify analysis host OS: Windows is not in this workflow's documented examples.' The generic question stores only field/message, and answerButton always calls focusAnswer for that field. It offers no direct compatibility evidence action. Source corroborates the focus behavior; clicking that particular button was not performed in this lane.
findings.impact: The reader has a real constraint, not a missing answer. Returning them to the unchanged selector does not explain how to verify compatibility, although the general tool-profile link remains available.
findings.confidence: High for observed message/action mapping; medium for reader friction.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish missing-answer and external-verification questions. Missing-answer actions should keep focusing fields; external verification should link to the tool's relevant compatibility notes/evidence and explain that a documented alternative host can be selected only if it matches the intended environment.
acceptance_criteria: An unknown host still produces an action to supply the host.
A known host outside documented examples links to compatibility notes and retains conditional status.
Do not let a user override undocumented compatibility into a verified match.
Explicit exclusions remain blocked; no widening of workflow support occurs.
Existing v1 system files remain unchanged.
findings.prior_audit_status: New next-step refinement; current uncertainty and platform rules are correct.
findings.compatibility: Internal question/action metadata only; preserve saved profile schema.

findings.title: Provide a reusable decision record between shortlist and execution
findings.user_task: Hand an analysis plan for several components to a teammate and later explain why each tool was selected.
findings.evidence: The UI explicitly states exports contain the system description, not candidates, match explanations, comparison selections or results. Live reload preserved the description and cleared the temporary shortlist. A comparison URL preserves up to three tool IDs, but not component/workflow roles or the rationale for choosing them. Free-text component notes already allow a manual workaround.
findings.impact: Reusable project descriptions exist, but the selected analysis approach and outstanding verification work are not captured in a maintained decision format.
findings.confidence: High for current behavior; medium for demand. This is intentional scope, not data loss.
findings.recommendation: Start with a lightweight human-readable adoption-note template linked from the builder, using component/connection, chosen tool and workflow, purpose, prerequisites, unresolved caveats, rationale, and evidence date. Reuse the run-record format for actual results later. A generated snapshot can follow demonstrated demand; do not increase the comparison-table limit or change existing export semantics merely to implement this.
acceptance_criteria: A multi-component plan can record complementary roles without claiming measured coverage.
Distinguish selected decisions from recomputed current candidates and executed results.
Existing description exports continue importing unchanged.
Do not silently persist currently temporary comparison choices.
Link source profiles and review dates so decisions can be revisited.
findings.effort: small for template; later UI generation optional and separately scoped
dependencies: Coordinate with REX-04 to share evidence conventions
findings.prior_audit_status: Related to previously proposed saved shortlists, narrowed to a documentation-first handoff.

strengths: Input/access distinctions prevented binary-only scenarios from implying instrumented builds.
Known incompatible Valgrind Windows route was excluded while unlisted-host examples stayed conditional.
Free and open-source preferences are distinct and were applied without borrowing paid edition capabilities.
The builder makes recommendation scope, temporary selections, and description-only exports explicit.
Java and temporal guides distinguish artifacts, assumptions and result types; dependency profiles distinguish inventory matches from source defects or demonstrated exploitability.
